Two fixes for clusters: coala-runtime's executor images are fetched from where they are published, and HDF5 works under the udocker engine.

## coala-runtime's executor images

`coala-runtime-python:latest` and `coala-runtime-r:latest` are local names: nothing publishes them under those names, so fetched as they are they resolve to `docker.io/library/…` and fail ("could not fetch docker.io/library/coala-runtime-python:latest … not found on Docker Hub"). coala-runtime hands the coala adapter where each is published, but only `ensure_image` used that, and coala-runtime never calls it: it calls `create_container`. The fetch had only worked where the image was already in the store.

`create_container` now calls `ensure_image` first. With coala-runtime 0.1.8, which publishes the images as `ghcr.io/coala-info/coala-runtime-{python,r}:latest`, an empty store pulls and tags them on first use.

## HDF5 under udocker

On hosts where only the udocker engine runs, every `h5py.File`, `anndata.read_h5ad` and scanpy read on a bind-mounted path failed with "Unable to synchronously open file (can't retrieve stat info for file)", in every Fakechroot mode. HDF5's default driver opens the file, then `lstat()`s its path to resolve symlinks. Fakechroot maps the open but not the stat call made by the HDF5 built into h5py's wheels, so it looked for the container path on the host.

Containers run under udocker now get `HDF5_DRIVER=stdio` unless you set it. HDF5 1.14 and later read it as the default driver, and the stdio driver skips that check. Other code built against an older glibc can hit the same gap; the README lists it under the udocker limits.

## Documentation

The README's examples use the ghcr.io image names, and the cluster section describes the automatic node-local container folder from 0.1.6.
